name: Skull Window
subtitle: a helmet microscope that sees neurons through bone

effects.effect: a laser makes sodium atoms high in the sky glow as an artificial star for correcting blur

effect: a laser makes sodium atoms high in the sky glow as an artificial star for correcting blur
how: The only ways to watch single brain cells today need a hole in the skull, so precise brain-computer interfaces mean surgery. A focused spot of ultrasound inside the head marks the light passing through it, acting like the artificial star astronomers use to correct the sky's blur; a camera works out how bone and tissue scrambled that light, and a shaped laser beam undoes the scramble to bring light to a sharp focus on neurons beneath the skull.
obstacle: Flowing blood re-scrambles the light within milliseconds, faster than today's corrections can keep up.
why: Guide-star focusing works through thin tissue; nothing images neurons through an adult skull.
real: Ultrasound-guide-star (TRUE) focusing works in brain tissue and other methods image through thin mouse skull, but no ultrasound-guided neuron imaging through an intact skull.
